# Azure Web PubSub Chat service client library for Java

[Azure Web PubSub Chat][product_documentation] is a managed chat capability built on [Azure Web PubSub][webpubsub_documentation]. It provides purpose-built client and server APIs for chat scenarios. Applications use the SDKs to work with chat-native concepts such as rooms, messages, members, and users. The service handles real-time message delivery and ordering, fan-out across a user's devices and browser tabs, room membership, and message persistence and retrieval.

Use this client library in an application server to:

- Create and manage Chat roles and permissions.
- Create users, rooms, and room memberships.
- Get room conversations and query persisted message history.
- Update and delete persisted messages.
- Generate client access credentials for Chat WebSocket clients.

[Source code][source_code] | [Package][package] | [API reference documentation][docs] | [Product documentation][product_documentation] | [Samples][samples] | [Changelog][changelog]

## Getting started

### Prerequisites

- A [Java Development Kit (JDK)][jdk] with version 8 or later.
- An [Azure subscription][azure_subscription].
- An [Azure Web PubSub resource][create_instance].
- A Web PubSub hub with [Chat enabled][enable_chat].

### 1. Add the package to your project

[//]: # ({x-version-update-start;com.azure:azure-messaging-webpubsub-chat;current})
```xml
<dependency>
    <groupId>com.azure</groupId>
    <artifactId>azure-messaging-webpubsub-chat</artifactId>
    <version>1.0.0-beta.1</version>
</dependency>
```
[//]: # ({x-version-update-end})

### 2. Create and authenticate a `WebPubSubChatServiceClient`

The client supports a connection string, an `AzureKeyCredential`, or a Microsoft Entra ID token credential. The hub passed to the client must have Chat enabled.

#### Use a connection string

Get the connection string from the Azure portal or Azure CLI, and store it securely. See [Web PubSub authorization][connection_string] for details.

```java readme-sample-createChatClientWithConnectionString
WebPubSubChatServiceClient client = new WebPubSubChatServiceClientBuilder()
    .connectionString("<web-pubsub-connection-string>")
    .hub("chat")
    .buildClient();
```

#### Use an access key

```java readme-sample-createChatClientWithKey
WebPubSubChatServiceClient client = new WebPubSubChatServiceClientBuilder()
    .endpoint("https://<resource-name>.webpubsub.azure.com")
    .hub("chat")
    .credential(new AzureKeyCredential("<web-pubsub-access-key>"))
    .buildClient();
```

#### Use Microsoft Entra ID

For recommended passwordless authentication, add the [Azure Identity][azure_identity] package, assign an appropriate Web PubSub data-plane role to the principal, and authenticate with a token credential. The following example uses `DefaultAzureCredential`:

```java readme-sample-createChatClientWithEntraId
WebPubSubChatServiceClient client = new WebPubSubChatServiceClientBuilder()
    .endpoint("https://<resource-name>.webpubsub.azure.com")
    .hub("chat")
    .credential(new DefaultAzureCredentialBuilder().build())
    .buildClient();
```

For more information, see [Authenticate Azure-hosted Java applications][azure_identity_auth] and [Microsoft Entra authorization for Azure Web PubSub][entra_authorization].

## Key concepts

### Client

`WebPubSubChatServiceClient` is the entry point for managing Chat resources in one Web PubSub hub. Create one client for each endpoint and hub combination, and reuse the client for multiple operations. For nonblocking operations, use `WebPubSubChatServiceAsyncClient`, which is created by calling `buildAsyncClient` on the same builder.

### Hub

A hub is a logical collection of WebSocket connections. A standard hub offers event-based real-time messaging through the Web PubSub subprotocol or a custom subprotocol. A chat hub adds built-in rooms, member management, message persistence, and chat-specific APIs.

This SDK applies only to chat hubs. Chat must be enabled on the target hub before the SDK can manage roles, users, rooms, members, conversations, or messages.

### Role and permission

A role is a named collection of Chat permissions. User role names start with `user.`, and room role names start with `room.`. Do not combine user and room permissions in one role.

User roles control operations such as creating rooms. Room roles control what a member can do in a particular room, such as publishing messages or reading message history. `BuiltInChatRoles` provides role names for common scenarios, and `ChatPermission` provides the permissions used to define custom roles.

### User

A user represents an application identity that can send and receive messages. A user is identified by a user ID and assigned a user role. A human user also has a nickname. Client access credentials associate WebSocket connections with a user ID.

### Room

A room groups users together and is the primary organizational unit for chat interactions. Every room has an automatically created default conversation.

### Room member

A room member represents a user added to a room. Membership controls which users can receive and send messages in the room. Each room member is assigned a room role.

### Conversation and message history

A conversation is a message thread that belongs to a room. Every room has a default conversation and can contain multiple conversations.

Messages sent to a conversation are delivered in real time to the room's connected members. The Chat service manages ordering and persistence, allowing members to load message history after reconnecting or joining later. The service client can list, update, and delete persisted messages.

### Client access credentials

`getClientAccessToken` returns a token and WebSocket connection URL. Clients configured with a connection string or access key sign the token locally. Clients configured with Microsoft Entra ID request the token from the Web PubSub service.

## Examples

### Generate a client access token

```java readme-sample-getChatClientAccessToken
WebPubSubClientAccessToken accessToken = client.getClientAccessToken(
    new GetClientAccessTokenOptions().setUserId("alice").setExpiresAfter(Duration.ofHours(1)));
String clientConnectionUrl = accessToken.getUrl();
```

The returned URL contains an access token. Send it only to the intended client, and do not log or persist it in production.

### Work with built-in values

```java readme-sample-chatBuiltInValues
String memberRole = BuiltInChatRoles.ROOM_MEMBER;
ChatPermission publishPermission = ChatPermission.ROOM_PUBLISH_MESSAGE;
```

### Create and list a custom role

```java readme-sample-manageChatRoles
ChatRole moderator = new ChatRole(Arrays.asList(ChatPermission.ROOM_HISTORY,
    ChatPermission.ROOM_REMOVE_USER, ChatPermission.ROOM_PUBLISH_MESSAGE));
client.createOrReplaceRole("room.moderator", moderator);

client.listRoles().forEach(role -> System.out.println(role.getName()));
client.deleteRole("room.moderator");
```

### Create a user, room, and room membership

```java readme-sample-manageChatRooms
client.createOrReplaceRole("user.room_creator",
    new ChatRole(Arrays.asList(ChatPermission.USER_CREATE_ROOM)));
client.createOrReplaceRole("room.contributor",
    new ChatRole(Arrays.asList(ChatPermission.ROOM_PUBLISH_MESSAGE)));
client.createOrReplaceUser("alice", new HumanChatUser("Alice", "user.room_creator"));

ChatRoom room = client.createOrReplaceRoom("general", new ChatRoom("General"));
ChatRoomMember member = client.createOrReplaceRoomMember(
    room.getId(), "alice", new ChatRoomMember("room.contributor"));
System.out.printf("%s: %s%n", member.getUserId(), member.getRoleName());

client.deleteRoom(room.getId());
client.deleteUser("alice");
client.deleteRole("room.contributor");
client.deleteRole("user.room_creator");
```

Delete dependent resources in reverse order when they are no longer needed: room, user, and then roles.

### List persisted messages

```java readme-sample-listChatMessages
ChatRoom room = client.getRoom("general");
client.listMessages(room.getDefaultConversation()).forEach(message ->
    System.out.printf("%s: %s%n", message.getCreatedBy(), message.getContent().getText()));
```

### Use the asynchronous client

```java readme-sample-createAsyncChatClient
WebPubSubChatServiceAsyncClient asyncClient = new WebPubSubChatServiceClientBuilder()
    .connectionString("<web-pubsub-connection-string>")
    .hub("chat")
    .buildAsyncClient();

asyncClient.listRoles().subscribe(role -> System.out.println(role.getName()));
```

### Service API versions

The client library targets the latest service API version by default. To use another supported version, pass a `WebPubSubChatServiceVersion` to the builder's `serviceVersion` method. Verify that the selected version supports the operations and models used by your application.

## Troubleshooting

### Handle service errors

Service operations throw `HttpResponseException` or a more specific subclass when a request fails. Inspect the status code and response body before retrying an operation. For example, a missing resource results in a `ResourceNotFoundException`, while a failed ETag condition can result in a `ResourceModifiedException`.

### Logging

Enable SDK logging by setting the `AZURE_LOG_LEVEL` environment variable. See [Azure SDK logging][logging] for the supported levels and logging configuration. HTTP logs can contain sensitive information. Do not enable detailed logging in production without reviewing how logs are collected and protected, and never log connection strings, access keys, bearer tokens, or generated client access tokens.

### Authentication and authorization

- Confirm that the endpoint and hub name identify the Web PubSub resource and Chat-enabled hub you intend to use.
- For Microsoft Entra ID, confirm that the principal has an appropriate Web PubSub data-plane role and that role assignment propagation has completed.
- Connection-string and access-key authentication are unavailable when local authentication is disabled on the Web PubSub resource.


## Next steps

Explore the [complete package samples][samples] to learn how to:

- Authenticate with a connection string, access key, or Microsoft Entra ID.
- Manage roles, permissions, users, rooms, and room members.
- Generate client access credentials.
- Query, update, and delete message history.
- Use synchronous and asynchronous clients.

proposals.subtype: Key credential and connection string builder traits
proposals.explanation: The script adds AzureKeyCredentialTrait<WebPubSubChatServiceClientBuilder> and ConnectionStringTrait<WebPubSubChatServiceClientBuilder> when absent. The captured credential(AzureKeyCredential) implementation rejects null and stores the key credential.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: WebPubSubChatCustomization explicitly inserts both interfaces into the generated builder; the captured unannotated credential setter implements the key trait.

proposals.subtype: Protocol token generation methods removed from public clients
proposals.explanation: The script removes generateClientToken and generateClientTokenWithResponse methods from both public clients and removes their GenerateClientTokenResponse import. The captured public token entry points instead return WebPubSubClientAccessToken through the token factory.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: These are explicit method removals in a Customization subclass, corroborated by the supplied replacement token entry-point bodies; no whole-client replacement is claimed.

proposals.subtype: Endpoint, key and optional port parsed from connection string
proposals.explanation: connectionString parses semicolon-separated settings, requires endpoint and accesskey, creates an AzureKeyCredential, validates the endpoint as a URL and optionally overrides its port. The parser splits at the first equals sign, trims values, normalizes keys to lowercase, ignores malformed entries and rejects duplicate normalized keys.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The script adds ConnectionStringTrait, and the captured builder implements its concrete parsing and credential/endpoint configuration rather than merely declaring a trait.

proposals.subtype: Key-signed bearer authentication or token credential policy
proposals.explanation: createHttpPipeline selects WebPubSubAuthenticationPolicy when a key credential is set, otherwise a bearer-token policy for a token credential, and throws when neither is available. The key policy generates a one-hour token using the outgoing request URL as audience and sets Authorization: Bearer only when token generation returns non-null.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The generated builder is explicitly extended for key authentication by the script, and the captured builder branch installs a dedicated non-generated WebPubSubAuthenticationPolicy whose body implements request-URL token authentication.

proposals.subtype: Request endpoint rewritten to configured reverse proxy
proposals.explanation: The reverseProxyEndpoint option installs ReverseProxyPolicy, which constructs the target URL from the configured proxy endpoint plus the original path and query, copies the request, replaces its URL in the context and advances a cloned next policy.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: A dedicated non-generated policy explicitly performs URL rewriting and is connected to the captured unannotated builder option and pipeline branch.

proposals.subtype: Client connection token and WebSocket URL
proposals.explanation: The sync and async token APIs use a factory that either requests a token from the service when no key is present or signs locally with the key. It uses fixed getGroupState/setGroupState roles, optional userId and clientType=default, validates that the lifetime in whole minutes is between one and Integer.MAX_VALUE, constructs the /client/hubs/<hub> audience, changes http to ws and appends the token as access_token in the returned URL.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The script removes the generated public token methods; captured added entry points invoke a dedicated non-generated factory containing the complete credential dispatch, option mapping, validation and URL construction.

proposals.subtype: HS256 JWT signing with key credentials
proposals.explanation: generateToken builds a JWT with audience, expiration, an optional subject and role claims, signs it with HS256 using UTF-8 bytes of the credential key, and serializes it. JOSEException is logged and returns null.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The complete non-generated token generator contains explicit JWT claim assembly and signing and is called by both the supplied request authentication policy and client token factory; this is not inferred from the JWT package dependency.

proposals.subtype: Public token options and connection result models
proposals.explanation: GetClientAccessTokenOptions exposes mutable userId and expiresAfter with fluent setters and a one-hour default lifetime. WebPubSubClientAccessToken holds final token and URL fields initialized through its public constructor and exposes read-only getters.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The complete unannotated public model classes directly support the separately implemented token factory and its replacement public API instead of exposing the internal GenerateClientTokenResponse.

proposals.explanation: BuiltInChatRoles exposes USER_NORMAL=user.normal, ROOM_MEMBER=room.member and ROOM_OPERATOR=room.operator as public static final string constants and has a private constructor.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The supplied complete class is an unannotated, non-generated named-constant utility alongside the dedicated token API models, rather than a generated extensible enum.

decisions.reason: The customization script explicitly adds both credential-related interfaces to the builder, and the supplied key-credential setter stores the validated credential. This is a public builder contract change, not a whole-client replacement.

The cited script removes generated token methods to make way for the separately proposed public access-token behavior. Counting that removal as an additional customization would count the replacement wiring rather than another independently implemented behavior; the new token API is assessed under its own key.

The complete setter and parser excerpts show concrete connection-string handling: normalized keys, duplicate detection, required endpoint and key, credential construction, URL validation and optional port replacement. The script explicitly adds the corresponding builder trait.
The credential-dependent pipeline branch and dedicated key policy are supported. The source masks the Authorization prefix, so the proposed literal header value cannot be asserted.

finding.subtype: Credential-dependent key-token or bearer authentication policy
finding.explanation: The builder installs WebPubSubAuthenticationPolicy for a key credential, otherwise BearerTokenAuthenticationPolicy for a token credential, and rejects a missing credential. The dedicated key policy generates a one-hour token for the request URL and, when non-null, writes it into the Authorization header with a prefix whose literal content is masked in the supplied evidence.
finding.handwrittenRationale: The script adds the key-credential builder trait, and the supplied standalone policy class implements the per-request key-token behavior used by the builder's credential branch; this is behavior beyond interface wiring.

decisions.reason: Rewriting outgoing request URLs for a reverse proxy is endpoint routing, not a convenience method. The existing endpoint-normalization pattern fits the actual policy implementation.

finding.subtype: Requests routed through configured reverse proxy
finding.explanation: The builder accepts a reverse-proxy endpoint and installs a policy that appends the outgoing URL's path and query to that endpoint, copies the request, replaces its URL and continues the pipeline.
finding.handwrittenRationale: The unannotated public builder option and the supplied standalone policy class implement the URL rewrite; the builder excerpt explicitly installs that policy when an endpoint is configured.

decisions.reason: Both public entry points delegate to the supplied standalone factory, which demonstrably chooses local signing or a service request, validates and maps options, and returns a token and WebSocket URL. The behavior is distinct from merely removing generated methods.

The signing implementation is supported, but this evidence does not establish that the service-specific JWT claim and key scheme could be inferred or produced by a general generator feature. Preserve the reusable JWT-signing pattern and mark addressability unclear.

finding.subtype: HS256 JWT creation from a key credential
finding.explanation: The token generator builds a JWT with audience, expiration and optional subject and role claims, signs it using HS256 and UTF-8 bytes from the supplied key credential, and returns the serialized token; it logs a JOSEException and returns null.
finding.handwrittenRationale: The standalone unannotated token generator explicitly assembles claims and signs a JWT, and the supplied policy and access-token factory call it; this is not inferred solely from a dependency.

decisions.reason: This groups two independently defined public model types with different roles into one instance. The input options and token/URL result deserve separate candidate findings with their own stable path-and-symbol identities, listed as omissions pending independent assessment.

The complete class defines public role-name constants but does not override a generated model. Classify the actual API addition as Other rather than Model overrides, retaining the existing constant-definition pattern.

finding.explanation: BuiltInChatRoles declares public static final strings USER_NORMAL, ROOM_MEMBER and ROOM_OPERATOR for the corresponding role names, and prevents instantiation with a private constructor.
finding.handwrittenRationale: The supplied complete class has neither a generator header nor Generated annotations, and the README names BuiltInChatRoles as the public role-name source; its declared constants are not a generated model override.

omissions.subtype: Public options for client access token creation
omissions.explanation: GetClientAccessTokenOptions supplies a one-hour default lifetime and fluent setters and getters for the expiration duration and optional user ID consumed by the token factory.
omissions.handwrittenRationale: This complete public options class has no generator header or Generated annotations and supplies the values consumed by the separately evidenced token factory; its provenance remains a candidate pending independent assessment.

omissions.subtype: Public client access token and URL result
omissions.explanation: WebPubSubClientAccessToken stores a token and client connection URL from its public constructor and exposes both through read-only getters.
omissions.handwrittenRationale: This complete public result class has no generator header or Generated annotations; its token-and-URL form is used by the separately evidenced access-token factory and remains a candidate pending independent assessment.

ChatMessage and MessageContent excerpts contain only JSON merge-patch accessor callbacks, without surrounding generation annotations or proof of a script edit. They are not sufficient to classify as additional serialization changes.
The removed generateClientToken method signatures are not supplied; only the script's exact method-name selectors can be reported without inventing parameter lists.
The trailing-Javadoc-whitespace replacement is formatting only and is not counted. Ordinary user-agent, retry and logging policies in pipeline setup are not counted as service-specific changes.
The captured validateClient method has endpoint/hub checks but lacks a supplied edit or contrasting generation context sufficient to distinguish it from ordinary builder validation.
No uncaptured constructor, token-credential setter, generated operation implementation, paging behavior or complete client surface is inferred.
Coverage is partial: 22 of 30 eligible files were captured from 51 discovered files, so the supplied evidence cannot establish the absence of additional customization.

Most client and builder excerpts do not include whole-file generator headers or all neighboring member annotations; unannotated excerpt members and complete standalone classes are provenance signals, not conclusive proof of regeneration behavior.

The captured Authorization header expression contains a masked prefix; the exact prefix and its runtime behavior cannot be independently established from this evidence. No external URLs or source files were consulted.

A whitespace-only Javadoc rewrite is visible in the customization script, but the supplied lines show formatting rather than a distinct SDK behavior. Generated-model merge-patch snippets and generic builder validation/build methods lack evidence of independently handwritten behavior.
